local_cpu_contract.scope: Physical x86-32 instructions and qualified local CPU effects only; no Source reconstruction, whole-function equivalence, original handler ABI, or saved-label authentication.
local_cpu_contract.qualification: Each local statement is conditional on that instruction being reached and completing without a fault. Values are sampled at that instruction; 32-bit address/register arithmetic wraps modulo 2^32. No runtime reachability or successful memory access is established.

memory.sampling: Each encoded load, store, compare, stack access, or read-modify-write uses memory and register values at its own execution time. Earlier loads are not substituted across possibly aliasing stores or calls.
memory.segments: No explicit segment override occurs. Encoded memory with EBP/ESP base uses SS by default; other bases and no-base addresses use DS. Implicit stack accesses use SS. LEA computes the encoded effective address without reading the referenced memory.
memory.aliases: Distinct offsets and saved names do not establish disjoint objects. Stack writes and loads may alias each other or other accessible addresses.
memory.byte_registers: AL operations access the low eight bits of current EAX. Byte stores and tests do not widen into dword accesses.

calls.instruction: Every decoded E8 pushes its encoded next instruction address to SS:[ESP-4], decreases ESP by four, and transfers to its numeric rel32 target, conditional on successful execution.
calls.opaque_return_boundary: Whether a callee returns is unknown. If execution resumes at the encoded return site, all returned general registers (including EBP/ESP), flags, and memory are unconstrained here. No register preservation, stack balance, argument count, calling convention, provider identity, or semantic return type is inferred.
calls.subsequent_stack_adjustments: POP or ADD ESP after a call operates on the actual returned ESP. Its presence does not prove that the callee preserved a previous stack/frame or consumed any specific arguments.

flag_rules.preserve: MOV, MOVSX, LEA, PUSH, POP, JMP, Jcc, near CALL, LEAVE, and near RET do not themselves change arithmetic flags; opaque callees may change every returned flag.
flag_rules.arithmetic: ADD/SUB/CMP define arithmetic status flags from the encoded-width operation; CMP discards the result. INC/DEC update arithmetic status flags while preserving CF.
flag_rules.logical: AND/XOR/TEST clear CF and OF, set SF/ZF/PF from their encoded-width result, and leave AF undefined; TEST discards its result.

prefix_before_first_possible_call.stack: For entry ESP=T and EBP=B, the initial PUSH EBP writes B to SS:[T-4]; MOV EBP,ESP makes F=T-4. SUB ESP,0x2c and PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI leave ESP=T-0x3c if the prefix completes. This relation is not carried across an opaque call.
prefix_before_first_possible_call.selection: C07629 reads ECX from SS:[F+0xc]; C0762D reads EBX from SS:[F+0x18]; C07630 reads EAX from DS:[EBX+4]. CMP EAX,0x80 controls C0763E JG because intervening PUSH/PUSH/MOV preserve those flags. The taken edge reads a dword from DS:[ECX+8]; the other edge sign-extends a byte from DS:[ECX+8].
prefix_before_first_possible_call.range_branch: The selected ECX is stored to SS:[F-8] at C0764C. Signed ECX<-1 reaches E8 at C07655. Otherwise signed ECX<EAX branches to C0765A; the remaining case reaches that E8. These are numeric local branches, not authenticated EH-state validation.

saved_override_sites.contract: Physical E9 transfers without pushing a return address or modifying arithmetic flags. Saved CALL_RETURN does not convert it into an E8 call, prove target behavior, or create a physical gap.
Physical E8 pushes C0779A. Saved CALL_RETURN does not prove nonreturn; a returned state at C0779A remains opaque. The next bytes are present and independently decoded.

suffix_if_reached.contract: From current ESP=S and EBP=F, successive POP EDI/ESI/EBX read SS:[S], SS:[S+4], SS:[S+8]. LEAVE then sets ESP to the current F, reads the replacement EBP from SS:[F], and advances ESP to F+4. RET reads the next EIP from SS:[F+4] and advances ESP to F+8. These instructions themselves preserve arithmetic flags. All reads occur in sequence; no relationship to original entry values or a restored caller is proved.
